summary: The improved 4-phase search algorithm achieved 100% coverage of the reference Pareto front (26/26 configs at seed=42, 28/28 at seed=123) within 200 evaluations, exceeding the ≥92% target. Full coverage was actually reached at just 100 evaluations, meaning the algorithm is twice as efficient as required. The original research question about search coverage is now fully answered.
key_points: Coverage improved from 84.6% (22/26) in iter-1 to 100% (26/26) in iter-2, a 15.4 percentage point gain, confirmed at two independent seeds.

Saturation occurs much earlier than predicted: 100% coverage is reached at budget=100 evals, not 200 — the first two phases (ceiling+cheapest scan, then boundary mapping) together cover all reference Pareto configs within ~60 evaluations.

Key structural facts now established: the Pareto-relevant KV cache space is only kv ∈ {2000, 3000, 4000, 5000} (kv=7500 and kv=10000 are never Pareto-optimal); bs=32 dominates (25/26 configs); 50% of Pareto configs involve preemption.
Still unknown: whether these structural findings (kv ceiling at 5000, bs=32 dominance, saturation budget) generalize to different models, request rates, or hardware configurations.

Recommended next iteration (iter-3): test robustness of the search algorithm and space structure across at least 2 different model/rate combinations to determine if the findings are workload-specific or general.
